French authorities have imposed overnight curfews in Paris and several other cities following a weekend of nationwide protests that descended into widespread rioting and looting. More than 2,500 people have been arrested, with at least two deaths reported and around 1,000 police officers injured. More than 2,000 businesses were affected, with damage estimated at hundreds of millions of euros. ... Italy’s government plans to deploy 500 troops to Milan after weekend protests over rising living costs and public services descended into rioting and looting. Deputy Prime Minister Matteo Salvini announced the move as luxury retailers boarded up windows and removed merchandise. Police arrested 32 people, most of them minors, while a business association estimated damage exceeding €1 million. ... Ukraine’s 92nd Separate Assault Brigade says it has evacuated a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone, in what it describes as a world first. The soldier was lifted by an Ayudag-6 hexacopter and taken to a safer position, where comrades arranged his transfer to hospital. He is now undergoing treatment and rehabilitation. The brigade said enemy drone activity and landmines had made evacuation by conventional unmanned ground vehicles impossible. Manufacturer Gurzuf Defence said the soldier had spent almost 18 months in a dangerous combat position and that reaching him would have exposed rescuers to deadly risks. Operators had to ensure the aircraft could carry a person without tipping or swaying excessively. ... Both Ukraine and Russia rely extensively on battlefield drones, creating areas where movement carries substantial danger. Ukraine has previously used unmanned ground vehicles to retrieve casualties but this is its first reported aerial evacuation. Australian independent MP Helen Haines remains in critical but stable condition after a driver allegedly struck her with a vehicle outside her electorate office in Wangaratta, Victoria, on Monday. Ms. Haines has lost one leg already as a result of the attack and doctors are fighting to save the other one. Witnesses said the vehicle turned towards the 65-year-old lawmaker before hitting her. Haines was airlifted to Melbourne. A 43-year-old man remains in custody. Police believe he acted alone. Helen Haines ... The attack has renewed concerns about threats against Australia’s accessible politicians. Australian Security Intelligence Organisation chief Mike Burgess warned that growing grievance and polarisation had created conditions more conducive to violence. Federal police recorded 1,067 reports of threatening or offensive behaviour towards political office holders and related premises in 2025-26, more than 10% above the previous year. A Houthi ballistic missile attack on a training camp in Yemen’s Shabwa province killed at least 53 security recruits and wounded more than 200 on Monday, local authorities said. The Saudi-backed government said three missiles struck the facility near Ataq; Houthi military spokesman Yahya Sarea claimed it housed Saudi forces. Yemen’s Presidential Leadership Council chairman Rashad al-Alimi promised a firm response. ... At least 73 people were killed and 19 wounded in a drone attack on a market in Abyei, the disputed region jointly administered by Sudan and South Sudan, according to caretaker information minister Yohana Akol Ngor. He accused Sudan’s army of Monday’s strike but provided no evidence. South Sudan summoned Sudan’s ambassador in protest, while medical charity Médecins Sans Frontières said it was treating more than 20 wounded patients. ... The attacks highlight the growing civilian toll of drone warfare. Between January and April, drones accounted for at least 880 civilian deaths in Sudan, more than 80% of conflict-related civilian fatalities during that period. US President Donald Trump said he would consider a three-way summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping, but insisted its focus should be nuclear disarmament rather than Ukraine. Putin reportedly proposed talks alongside next month’s APEC summit in China to discuss ending the war. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed discussions about a meeting but said neither its format nor agenda was settled. ... A summit among the three nuclear powers could open discussions on arms controls but the prospect has raised concerns about allies being excluded from decisions affecting their security. The proposed meeting remains uncertain, as does whether Ukraine would feature in any eventual talks. The World Food Programme has cut monthly food assistance in Gaza from 1.6 million people to 1.1 million after its funding fell to less than half previous levels. Families now receive one food parcel instead of two, cash payments have been reduced, and daily hot meals have fallen from 250,000 to 150,000. The agency warns that recent improvements in food security could quickly reverse. ... Around 1.4 million people, or 67% of Gaza’s population, still face crisis-level hunger or worse, including 200,000 in emergency conditions. More than 80% of residents are unemployed, leaving many unable to buy food even when it is available. ... World Food Programme Palestine director Shaun Hughes said recovery investment was essential because the humanitarian operation was unsustainable. Reconstruction promised after the October 2025 ceasefire has not begun. The agency needs $450 million to maintain critical operations across Gaza and the West Bank through March. Japan launched its Martian Moons Exploration spacecraft aboard an H3 rocket on Tuesday, beginning a five-year mission to collect samples from Phobos, the larger of Mars’ two moons. The spacecraft separated successfully after launch from Tanegashima Island. No mission has previously returned material from Mars or either moon, and earlier attempts to reach Phobos have failed. ... The spacecraft is expected to reach Mars next year. A French-German rover named Idefix will survey Phobos for 100 days before a Japanese lander attempts to collect at least 10 grams of ... US President Donald Trump’s approval rating has fallen to 31%, the lowest of either presidential term, as rising fuel prices weigh on voters ahead of November’s congressional elections. A Reuters/Ipsos poll found 47% of registered voters favour Democrats against 35% for Republicans, widening the opposition’s lead from seven to 12 percentage points in two weeks. The shift follows the US-Israeli war against Iran, which began in February and drove up petrol prices. Some 68% disapprove of Trump’s handling of the economy, including 37% of Republicans. Women favour Democratic congressional candidates by 50% to 32%.

items.title: U.S. Treasury yields fall as investors await housing, employment data
items.excerpt: U.S. Treasury yields inched lower on Tuesday as investors awaited further economic data and continued to weigh the inflationary backdrop ahead of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision next week. The benchmark 10-year Treasury Add To Watchlist yield was down 2 basis points to 5.114%, while the 30-year Treasury Add To Watchlist bond also fell 2 basis points to 5.45%. Meanwhile, the 2-year Treasury Add To Watchlist note yield was broadly flat at 4.757%. One basis point is equal to 0.01%, and yields and prices move in opposite directions. Investors will parse housing starts and monthly pending home sales data for September, due later on Tuesday morning, and weekly ADP employment change figures. ... Weekly initial jobless claims will be released on ... Investors are anticipating the Fed's next interest rate decision, due next week. The latest figures for the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, the personal consumption expenditures index, will also be released. Traders are now pricing in an 82% chance of the Fed holding interest rates steady, according to the CME FedWatch Tool.

items.title: Inflation jumps to 3.7% as gas, diesel prices squeeze consumers
items.excerpt: Prices rose across broad swaths of the U.S. economy in September as high energy costs triggered by the Iran war pushed up prices in many major consumer categories. The Bureau of Labor Statistics said Wednesday that overall prices rose 3.7% from a year ago and 0.6% from August. Categories including housing, clothing, and restaurant and takeout food all saw price increases. Only three major categories saw price declines: groceries, medical care commodities and utility gas service. ... Since August, oil prices have risen to more than $106 per barrel from about $80. The price of unleaded gas, which most consumers use, has risen 45% since late February, when the United States and Israel launched the Iran war. The price of diesel, which powers businesses, farms, the shipping industry and other critical sectors, has soared 70% over the same period. ... Stocks fell sharply Wednesday. Before the data, market odds showed that traders had expected the Federal Reserve to wait until December to raise rates. After the data, odds rose above 55% for an October hike. The Nasdaq Composite closed down 1.8%, and the S&P 500 tumbled 1.1%. The Russell 2000 index, which tracks small and medium-size companies, slid 1.9%. The stocks that sold off the most were interest rate sensitive, such as those in the technology and industrial sectors, which are involved in the ever-expanding AI data center build-out. ... The artificial intelligence boom also reared its head last month, as categories that track the price of computers, software and accessories posted record year-over-year price increases. Ahead of Wednesday’s report, economists had been watching recent price hikes on Apple products and whether they have an impact on the overall inflation figure. The smartphone category rose 0.4% month over month. Airline fares were also being closely watched, given soaring jet fuel costs. Prices in that category rose 0.2% from August, posting their smallest increase since June.

items.title: Hassett Says CPI Data Shows Inflation Needs ‘Some Work’
items.excerpt: (Bloomberg) -- White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett said prices have been falling for items such as beef and eggs, though consumer price data for September shows overall inflation continues to need policy attention. "If you look at the previous three months, it looked like inflation was completely under control, and now it looks like it's sort of back needing some work," Hassett told CNBC Monday. Data last week showed consumer prices advanced in September at the fastest pace in five months and a gauge of underlying price pressures rose by more than expected. The consumer price index rose 0.6% from a month earlier while a key measure of underlying price pressures, which excludes food and energy, was up 0.3%. "This is either a sort of break from the downtrend or a blip," Hassett said in the interview. Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh last week did nothing to dispel market expectations that the central bank will hold interest rates steady when it meets at the end of the month. In a moderated discussion at the International Monetary Fund's annual meetings, Warsh made no remarks on monetary policy or his outlook for the US economy, apart from reiterating that the Fed will deliver price stability. Hassett said he respects the central bank's independence and said Warsh will "do what he thinks is the right thing." ... "People are really euphoric about how well the economy is doing, and they're spending more. And of course, that's the kind of thing the Fed needs to pay attention to," Hassett said.

items.title: US midterms: Iran war and cost of living put Trump's foreign ...
items.excerpt: - US foreign policy, particularly the Iran war, is playing an unusually prominent role in the 2026 midterm elections. - Petrol prices have risen nearly 50 per cent and diesel by two thirds since the war against Iran began in February. - Democrats have an 85 per cent chance of winning the House, though flipping the Senate remains a significantly harder task. - A Reuters/Ipsos poll found Mr Trump's approval rating at a record low of 31 per cent, driven largely by economic discontent. US foreign policy is playing an outsized role in this year's midterm elections, thanks largely to President Donald Trump's war against Iran and its effect on the cost of living for Americans. Republicans control both chambers of Congress, and Democrats are trying to win back some power on November 3, having spent two years in the political wilderness after a disastrous performance during the 2024 presidential election. ... A Democratic victory in either chamber would give the opposition greater powers to oppose Mr Trump's agenda, and the ability to launch investigations and call witnesses to testify about action the administration has taken. Recent polling gives the Democrats a more-than 85 per cent chance of winning the House, where they only need to flip a handful of seats. The Senate is a trickier task for Democrats, who need to gain four seats to secure a majority, including at least two in states Mr Trump carried by double digits in 2024. ... Front and centre of many political debates in the US is the cost of living, particularly petrol prices, which have risen by nearly 50 per cent since Mr Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu launched their war against Iran on February 28. Diesel, the lifeblood of the trucking industry, has been even harder hit, having risen by about two thirds. Costs for farmers, truckers and businesses have soared, with high prices being passed on to consumers in many instances.

It also comes after President Trump floated resuming military operations against Iran following next month's U.S. midterm elections. Hegseth confirmed in an X post that he was in U.S. Central Command's area of responsibility on Monday, sharing a photo of himself addressing American service members who he said were "on a historic mission." The order gives the National Institutes of Health 90 days to create a new women’s health division. It will work alongside an office that has focused on women’s health since 1990. The order sets no specific funding amount for the research. Non-citizen voter roundup » Federal agents arrested 11 non-citizens in California on Monday in a crackdown on illegal voting in US elections. WORLD’s Harrison Watters has more. HARRISON WATTERS: The Department of Justice says those arrested are among 28 green-card holders now charged with election-related crimes. Prosecutors accuse many of fraudulently registering to vote and illegally casting ballots. The DOJ last week asked California to review its voter rolls for around 20,000 individuals the federal government suspects are noncitizens. And the department wants the state to set aside their mail ballots until they’re verified as eligible to vote. State officials, though, declined to meet the two-day deadline. Critics of the crackdown say non-citizen voter fraud is rare and highly unlikely to decide an election. But DOJ official Trent McCotter said—his words— “Every illegal vote cancels out the vote of a lawful American citizen.” ... Ebola update » More than $700 million meant to fight Ebola in Congo is missing in the financial reports provided by aid groups. That's according to authorities there who say they've launched an investigation and are demanding answers. Meanwhile, the outbreak is still spreading. It has now reached an eighth province in Congo. Officials report more than 4,500 deaths since May, making this the country’s deadliest Ebola outbreak. And Kenya has now confirmed eight cases. The latest patient tested positive while already in quarantine. Health officials say there’s still no evidence the virus is spreading in the wider community. Houthis strike government military camp » In Yemen, missiles struck a military training camp Monday, killing at least 53 government recruits. WORLD’s Kristen Flavin has more. KRISTEN FLAVIN: Local officials say Houthi rebels launched the attack, which wounded another 200 people.

items.excerpt: NEW YORK (AP) — Beloved character actor Richard Riehle has died at 78. Wright Entertainment Inc. announced Monday that Riehle died on Oct. 15. Riehle's career spanned nearly five decades, with memorable roles in “Office Space,” “Glory,” and “The Fugitive.” He often played authority figures but was equally skilled in comedy. He began acting at the University of Notre Dame and later earned a Masters of Fine Arts from the University of Minnesota. Riehle appeared in three “Star Trek” series and on Broadway. He is remembered for his talent, kindness, and support for emerging actors. ... John Legend's new album titled “Muse,” produced by Pharrell Williams, is among the new streaming releases coming the week of Oct. 19. The live-action “Moana,” featuring Dwayne Johnson as Maui,” debuts Wednesday on Disney+. The original animated version is also available. On Friday, “The Invite,” starring Seth Rogen and Olivia Wilde, streams on HBO Max. In gaming, “Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4" launches Friday, this time set on the Korean Peninsula. “Nintendo Switch Sports Resort” arrives Thursday, offering 12 events including bowling and tennis for up to eight players online. New television series include the fourth season of Netflix's “Lupin” and a three-episode “Vanderpump Rules” series set in Las Vegas. ... Paramount's “Street Fighter” leads the box office this weekend, earning $31 million from 3,575 theaters in the U.S. and Canada. However, the spotlight is on the Elizabeth Holmes documentary “You Can See Everything,” which made an impressive $15 million from just 855 screens. Directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, the film has received rave reviews and a 99% rating on Rotten Tomatoes. Meanwhile, the survival thriller “Whalefall” underperformed, earning $8 million domestically. The weekend's overall ticket sales reached about $101.6 million, marking a 45% increase from last year. ... NEW YORK (AP) — Selma Blair's representatives have stated she did not intend to harm anyone during a recent flight incident. Blair, who has multiple sclerosis, experienced a medical emergency on a Delta flight from Los Angeles to New York. She was accused of injuring two flight attendants and later kicking a police officer and a nurse. Her representatives emphasized that Blair's condition can cause episodes that may be misunderstood. Blair pleaded not guilty to assault charges and is free on bail. The FBI has also charged her with assault related to her actions on the plane. Blair has been a vocal advocate for disability rights. ... NEW YORK (AP) — Superhero films and horror have usually stayed on separate sides of the multiplex. But DC Studios' “Clayface” is the rare attempt to meld the two movie genres. “Clayface” is something unusual in the normally calculated realm of comic book movies. It’s R-rated. It’s also modestly budgeted at $40 million. And it stars the relatively unknown Tom Rhys Harries as a little-known DC villain. And it comes at a pivotal time for James Gunn and Peter Safran's DC Studios, following the box-office flop of “Supergirl” and the Warner Bros. merger with Paramount. ... “La Bola Negra” is a Spanish flim that explores the lives of gay men in Spain in 1932, 1937 and 2017. Directed by Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvo, the film draws inspiration from Federico García Lorca and Alberto Conejero’s works. It weaves stories of love, war and generational trauma, featuring a standout debut by Guitarricadelafuente. In her review for The Associated Press, film writer Lindsey Bahr writes that the film, despite some stylistic weight, is a remarkably transfixing exercise and exploration of the caustic ripple effects of repression and silence. Rated R, the film is in theaters now and will be on Netflix in December.
